title: Parallel sentences: English and Spanish prompts

fields.name: id
fields.description: Stable id, never reused. The hold-out is decided from it: the prompt belongs in eval/parallel/ when int(sha256(id), 16) mod 100 < 15.

fields.name: text
fields.description: The prompt: one everyday sentence of 1 to 14 words, with no digits and no abbreviations (Common Voice sentence rules)

fields.name: topic
fields.description: Everyday theme, e.g. home, school, shop, health, weather

fields.name: origin
fields.description: written: written for the project; tatoeba-cc0: from Tatoeba's CC0 export (only with the maintainer's approval of the download)

fields.name: origin_ref
fields.description: Id in the origin, e.g. the Tatoeba sentence id. Empty for prompts written for the project.

fields.name: author
fields.description: Who wrote the prompt: machine for a machine draft, otherwise handles from _meta/contributors.tsv, separated by '; '

fields.name: batch
fields.description: The batch the row arrived in: prompts-1, prompts-2 ... for prompts; contrib-YYYY-MM-DD for a contribution-tool sync. With translated_by or author it is the row's provenance.

fields.name: reviewed_by
fields.description: GitHub usernames of the review-board members who confirmed the row, separated by '; '. Required when status is reviewed.

$comment: For corpus/parallel/prompts.tsv and eval/parallel/prompts.tsv (the held-out split, never trained on). Prompts are English or Spanish, so they get no Aruban spelling checks, and they cite no source page: origin, author and batch are their provenance. CC0 1.0 (LICENSE-DATA). See _meta/conventions.md, Parallel sentences.
